explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is about objects the library defines itself: `curveField p`, `constantCompositum`, `sElement`, `genX` and `genY`. It says that a specific constant-field compositum equals `⊤` when p ≠ 2. The library's own proof places sElement, genY and genX in the compositum C and uses `X_eq_genY_div` to get X in C. It then uses `RatFunc.adjoin_X`: adjoining X over RatFunc (ZMod p) gives all of RatFunc (RatFunc (ZMod p)). The real content is in the library's definitions and auxiliary lemmas. Mathlib supplies only generic glue: `IntermediateField.adjoin_toSubfield`, `Subfield.closure_le`, `RatFunc.adjoin_X` and `eq_top_iff`. None of these states the theorem, and it is not a special case of any single one of them, so I did not need a wider search.
